data.description:
Server-side account capability, chain link 1 ("freelancer signs up"). Sign-up and sign-in with locally stored credentials (password hashing from the platform's own crypto primitives — no new dependency), session issuance and validation, a currentUser context for downstream handlers, and a route guard that every authenticated endpoint uses.

IMPLEMENTS: docs/engineering/00-d1-v1-milestone-plan.md section 3 row C-07 (IN — Rule 1, chain link 1). The screen that drives it is row C-08 and belongs to the onboarding-UI task.

DECISION CONTEXT. This is deliberately split from its screen so the server half is not blocked behind wireframes — see the milestone plan section 8.1 on how the UI and non-UI halves interleave, and section 8.4's ready-queue simulation, which depends on splits like this one. NO EMAIL IS INVOLVED: email verification, magic links, and password reset are OUT of v1 (row C-09, Rule 1, and independently Rule 3 — they need an ESP account and a sender domain, and the product has no name yet, per docs/strategy/09-company-name.md section 8.2, which extends "public-facing artifact" to sender-domain configuration). A v1 freelancer who forgets their password is a support case, not a feature; that capability returns with the email milestone (milestone plan section 6.2).

VERIFICATION: unit and HTTP-level tests — sign-up creates a user; sign-in issues a session; a guarded route rejects an absent, invalid, or expired session; credentials are never stored or logged in plaintext. No accounts, no network.

NOT IN THIS TASK: the sign-up/sign-in screen; password reset or any outbound email (out of v1); OAuth or social login (not a capability row — a v1 that needs no ESP needs no external identity provider either, and adding one would be a Rule-3 account); roles, teams, or multi-seat (row C-50, OUT).

data.body:
Pulled as the next D1 pull. Not the highest priority left on paper — AS-42 is also medium — but it is the one every UI task needs: AS-41 and AS-43 both carry an AS-40 OBLIGATION marker on the interim resolveFreelancerId seam, and all four screens assume a signed-in user. Landing it collapses two marked seams rather than adding a third.

Lena implements: Marcus wrote AS-41 and AS-43, which are the two callers of the seam this task replaces, and a fresh reader is more likely to notice if the replacement quietly changes their behaviour. She also owned the auth and session layer end to end at Harborview through a security audit, which is the closest prior experience anyone here has to this task.

Owen plans as tech lead. Note for the planner: no email exists in v1 by two independent rules, so there is no reset path — say what a forgotten password means operationally rather than leaving it implied.

Plan written (§0-§11, 1,460 lines). Four decisions with stated bases: scrypt N=2^14/r=8/p=1/keylen=32 (measured 39 ms median in the pinned amd64 image; 2^15 rejected because it exceeds Node's DEFAULT maxmem and throws — measured, so its failure mode under a forgotten argument is an outage rather than a slow hash); a server-side sessions row rather than a signed token, which makes this task carry migration 0002 and, deliberately, NO config row — there is nothing to sign, so config.test.js:37's SESSION_SECRET prediction is wrong and is corrected; SameSite=Lax (Strict would break Stripe's cross-site return redirect and silently kill chain link 2) plus a same-origin check on unsafe methods, no CSRF token, because a token would be four cross-task obligations on unplanned UI tasks; and the guard's reachability proven by walking the built app's routes against a committed list and driving a cookieless request at every protected one — verified express 5.2.1 exposes app.router in the real image. Both AS-40 OBLIGATION markers are deleted and resolveFreelancerId goes with them: the seam's replacement is its removal. ?freelancer= must die in the same merge — leaving it live alongside sessions is an impersonation hole (G13 tests it), which is why §8 declares the task explicitly not splittable at the seam. Measured while planning and easy to miss: test/webhooks.test.js line 784 also drives ?freelancer= (so it is in scope), and test/invoices.test.js is 20 lines under the 1,200-line cap.

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-40 on feat/AS-40-accounts, per the plan: scrypt at the measured 2^14 parameters with upgrade-on-login, migration 0002 for credentials and sessions with the two CHECK constraints, the positional guard boundary plus the router-tree reachability test, SameSite=Lax with the same-origin check, and deletion of both AS-40 OBLIGATION markers together with every ?freelancer= site in the same change.

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE — AS-40 (developer-lena). 6 commits on feat/AS-40-accounts, worktree clean, nothing pushed or merged.

== DIFF ==
30 files, +2636/-250 (plan §8 projected 30 files / ~2050 insertions). 10 new, 20 modified.
New: lib/auth/{password,session,accounts,guard}.js, lib/db/migrations/0002-accounts.js, lib/db/repositories/{credentials,sessions}.js, routes/auth.js, test/auth.test.js, test/helpers/auth.js.
Commits: c559bef schema+repositories | 7331874 sessions+guard+seam removal | de52ae8 README | 51a6206 engine-level CHECK assertions | f878bdd await/NUL/V4 | ff5aae1 A17/A18 layer discrimination. Each independently green; every moved literal in the same commit as its change.

== SUITES ==
test service (network_mode: none, mountless): 334 tests, 316 pass, 0 fail, 18 skipped.
contract service (stripe-mock): 334 tests, 334 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped — the 18 un-skip and pass, so AC 25 is measured rather than claimed.
THE 18 SKIPS, enumerated — all are ASC_STRIPE_MOCK_URL self-skips, no other skip mechanism fires: connect M1/M2/M3; invoices M1/M2/M3; stripe-mock.test.js's 12 (reachable-and-not-Stripe, strict-version-check, connected POST /v1/customers, /v1/invoiceitems, /v1/invoices, /v1/invoices/{id}/finalize, /v1/invoices/{id}/send, GET /v1/invoices/{id}, the three platform calls, unknown-parameter rejection, Idempotency-Key echo, forbidden-shape refusal).

== FALSIFICATION: 13 recipes, all run against a `git archive HEAD` extract OUTSIDE the worktree ==
Method: 461-file content-hash manifest of the pristine extract; each recipe gets a fresh copy verified against all 461 hashes BEFORE mutating (so no recipe can inherit another's damage); mutation asserts applied ON DISK against a measured baseline (script exits non-zero otherwise) AND INSIDE THE BUILT IMAGE; suite run; copy discarded.
RESTORATION: the worktree was never the mutation target, so restoration is not something I undid — it is something that was never at risk. Proven three ways: `git -C <wt> status --porcelain` empty, `git diff --exit-code` and `--cached --exit-code` both clean, and a manifest re-derived from HEAD after the last recipe is byte-identical to the one taken before the first (461/461).

F1  discard-hash removed (MUTANT-F1 0->1; hasher.hashPassword( 4->3) -> EXACT {A12}. AS PREDICTED. No H-case moved — H8 (byte-identical responses) stayed green, which is the confirming signal the plan asked for: the enumeration answer is carried by work done, not by a response difference.
F2  requireSameOrigin unmounted -> EXACT {G9–G12}. As predicted (plan named G10+G12 as separate cases; I wrote the four as one test, so this is a naming difference, not a behavioural one).
F3  safeNext returns its argument -> EXACT {H12–H15}. Same naming note.
F4  sessions CHECK deleted (NOT GLOB 1->0) -> EXACT {A18}. WIDER-THAN-NOTHING FINDING: see (1) below. D3/D4 stayed GREEN, contradicting the plan's prediction — see (2).
F5  sameSite lax->strict in setSessionCookie only (lax 2->1) -> {H2, H3, H4}. WIDER than the predicted {H4}: H2 and H3 also assert SameSite on the emitted header. H9 (clearCookie shape) stayed green, confirming the two literals really are independently mutable — which is why the plan wanted two.
F6  webhook mount moved below requireSession (line 87 -> 143, below requireSession at 129; app.use unchanged at 11) -> 23 red: G8 + W2,W3,W4a,W4b,W4c,W5,W6,W7,W8,W9,W10,W11,W12a,W12b,W13,W14,W15,W16,W17,W19,W20 + webhooks' own G3. WIDER than the plan's enumerated list, which omitted W3/W4a-c/W15/G3 — those expect 400, so they satisfy the plan's stated RULE ("every case expecting a status other than 303"); the enumeration was incomplete, not the rule. W1 and W18 stayed green. W1 is green for the RIGHT reason now, not the wrong one the plan predicted — see (7).
F7  credentials prefix assertion deleted -> EXACT {A17}. Only after the fix in (3); on first run it was GREEN, which is the finding.
F8  console.log(password) in signIn (console. 0->1) -> EXACT {A19, the concept-rows test}, two witnesses as predicted. This is the recipe behind AC 5.
F9a createHmac added to password.js (0->2; signature.js unchanged at 2/4) -> EXACT {concept rows}: "webhook signature HMAC: found in [lib/auth/password.js, lib/webhooks/signature.js], allowed in exactly [lib/webhooks/signature.js]".
F9b timingSafeEqual removed from password.js (3->0; signature.js unchanged at 4) -> EXACT {concept rows}, in the used-exemption direction: "constant-time compare: found in [lib/webhooks/signature.js], allowed in exactly [lib/auth/password.js, lib/webhooks/signature.js]". Both halves of the split guard shown firing in both directions: splitting it did not weaken it.
F10 invoiceRoutes moved above requireSession (app.use unchanged at 11) -> EXACT {G3, R20}. SECOND-ORDER EFFECT CONFIRMED: observed status is 500, not 200 — actingFreelancerId throws and the router error handler maps it. G1's route walk stayed GREEN, which is exactly why G3 exists and why the walk alone would not be enough.
F11 test/auth.test.js removed in the copy -> EXACT {harness V2}, message verbatim: "expected exactly 14 test files, found 13: assets.test.js, config.test.js, ... webhooks.test.js".
V1  ASC_SELFTEST_MUTATE=1 -> EXIT=1, EXACT {harness V1}.
V4  NUL byte planted in lib/auth/session.js -> EXACT {V4}, naming "lib/auth/session.js: byte 0x00 at offset 1947". Demonstrated alongside: `file` reports "data" and `grep -c TOKEN_BYTES` prints nothing and exits 1.

== FINDINGS ==
(1) FIVE OF MY OWN CASES WERE VACUOUS, and F4 is what caught them. Making withRepos async left A14–A18 calling it un-awaited: each test returned undefined, node reported green, and the assertions ran afterwards. Under F4, A18 showed a TICK while its real failure arrived as an unhandledRejection after the test ended. All five are now awaited (f878bdd).
(2) F4's predicted {A-repo case, D3, D4} is WRONG about D3/D4, and the reason is a real gap: db.test.js pins table/index/autoindex COUNTS and STRICT-ness, and D4's catalogue comparison is before-vs-after WITHIN one database — so nothing in the suite pins any migration's DDL TEXT. Deleting a CHECK constraint is invisible to db.test.js. The plan's "a run where only the A-repo case goes red means the catalogue assertions are not reading the migration they claim to" is exactly right, and that is what the run showed. Not fixed here (it is an AS-39-surface change); flagged for the reviewer.
(3) F7 RAN GREEN ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT — the finding, not a pass. A17/A18 half (a) asserted only the ERROR CLASS, and both layers raise ValidationError (lib/db/errors.js maps a CHECK refusal to one), so half (a) simply passed on the engine's answer and deleting the repository assertion reddened nothing. Fixed in ff5aae1 by asserting `field`: the repository names the input (passwordHash, id), the engine names the constraint (check). F7 now reddens exactly half (a); F4 reddens exactly half (b).
(4) TWO SOURCE FILES CARRIED A LITERAL NUL, written where an escape sequence was meant (lib/auth/guard.js, then test/auth.test.js). Both ran and passed their unit tests perfectly; the damage was invisible except through grep, which treats the file as binary — every match prints nothing and exits 1. This repo's whole mutation discipline rests on grep-based assert-applied steps, so I added V4 to harness.test.js (deviation 1) and falsified it.
(5) F2's stated baseline is UNRUNNABLE AS WRITTEN. `grep -c 'requireSameOrigin' app.js` is 3 on my HEAD (import line, an explanatory comment, the mount), not the plan's 1 — a `grep -c` counts LINES, and the plan's figure ignored the import it necessarily requires. Ran as 3->2 plus an exact check that `^  app.use(requireSameOrigin(config));$` went 1->0. This is the fifth recurrence of this defect class across four tasks.
(6) F6/F10's "app.use unchanged at 7 (E14)" cites MASTER's count as a POST-CHANGE invariant. The true post-change count is 11 (this task adds loadSession, requireSameOrigin, requireSession, authRoutes and removes none). Both recipes ran with 11 as the invariant, and it held.
(7) AC 17 AND AC 20 ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE AS WRITTEN. AC 17 requires G13 to send `?freelancer=<another id>`; AC 20 requires `grep -rn 'freelancer=' --include='*.js'` to return zero. G13 is the security test the whole seam replacement exists for, so it wins. See the seam section below for what I verified instead.
(8) TWO GENUINE DESIGN BUGS the plan did not anticipate, both fixed: (a) requireSession guarded /signin itself — since nothing serves that path until AS-45, every signed-out visitor fell through to the guard and was redirected to /signin, an INFINITE REDIRECT LOOP, and AS-45's screen would have redirected to itself on arrival. The guard now never guards the path it sends people to (G13b). (b) The plan's `password KDF` concept row fires on the migration and the credentials repository, which carry the stored-format prefix 'scrypt$' — its measured baseline of zero was taken on master, before this task introduced that prefix. I narrowed the PATTERN with a trailing (?!\$) rather than widening the allowlist: allowlisting those two files would let a real KDF call hide in either one.
(9) ORDERING CONSEQUENCE, worth a reviewer's eye: requireSameOrigin sits ABOVE the auth boundary and fails closed, so an unsafe request with no Origin and no Referer is 403 BEFORE the guard runs. The plan's §3.5.5 table ("any other method, no valid session -> 303") is true only for a request that carries an Origin — which a browser always does. This changed three shipped cases (connect R13, invoices R20, webhooks W1) and is documented in the README.

== THE SEAM: EXPLICIT CONFIRMATION ==
Commands run from apps/invoicing:
  grep -rn 'resolveFreelancerId' . --include='*.js' --exclude-dir=node_modules            -> 0
  grep -rn 'freelancer=' . --include='*.js' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=test -> 0
  grep -rn "searchParams.set('freelancer'" . --exclude-dir=node_modules                   -> 0
  grep -rn 'AS-40 OBLIGATION' . --exclude-dir=node_modules                                -> 0
  grep -rn 'req\.query|\.query\.' . --include='*.js' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=test -> 0
Measured baselines removed: resolveFreelancerId 12 lines / 4 files; freelancer= 63 lines / 5 files (including test/webhooks.test.js:784 and lib/connect/onboarding.js's searchParams.set, which a token search misses); AS-40 OBLIGATION 3.
ONE occurrence of `freelancer=` survives in *.js, deliberately: test/auth.test.js:895, which is G13's ATTACK PAYLOAD — the request that names another freelancer and must be ignored. Production source is at zero, and reads no query parameter at all.

== LITERALS ==
Moved: harness EXPECTED_TEST_FILES + 'auth.test.js' at index 1 and 13->14 (number, message, and the "thirteen files"->"fourteen" comment); dependency-policy source list 35->43 (8 new entries in sorted position) and its raw SQL row 9->12; body parser row + routes/auth.js; the webhook-HMAC row SPLIT into createHmac (still exactly one file) + constant-time compare (two files); 6 new concept rows; db.test.js's whole migration-2 set (TABLES +credentials/+sessions, NAMED_INDEXES +sessions_expires, D2 1->2 migrations and SCHEMA_VERSION 1->2, D3 tables 8->10 / named 4->5 / autoindexes 13->15 / ledger row, D4 catalogue 8+4+13 -> 10+5+15, **D5's from-the-future literal 2->3** (the least obvious one, and it is really SCHEMA_VERSION+1), D15's name and applied list); repositories.test.js Z3 seven->nine keys; config.test.js and lib/config.js comments (no assertion moved).
NOT moved, verified byte-identical vs master by git diff over the whole §2 list: server.js, Dockerfile, compose.yaml, package.json, package-lock.json, lib/health.js, 0001-initial.js, lib/db/errors.js, lib/db/connection.js, lib/stripe/*, lib/vendor.js, lib/views.js, lib/webhooks/*, lib/invoices/lifecycle.js, routes/{assets,pages,webhooks}.js, views/, public/, test/{deploy-shape,assets,stripe-client,stripe-mock}.test.js. SCHEMA.length still 11; LOCK_ENTRIES still 70; SANCTIONED still 3; money representation row unmoved (no new file contains a money word — checked RAW, comments included).

== DEVIATIONS (numbered) ==
1. ADDED test/harness.test.js V4 (no control bytes in any source file), ~30 lines, not in the plan. Justification: finding (4) — the same defect twice in one task, and it silently defeats every grep-based assert-applied step the house mutation discipline depends on. Placed in the vacuity-floor file, and falsified.
2. MODIFIED test/health.test.js, which §4.3 claims is unchanged. Only the two scaffold-PAGE cases folded into that file (GET / and the unknown-path 404) — both now sit behind the boundary and sign in first, because their claims are about rendering and routing, not auth. All four health checks and every health assertion are untouched; body.checks.length is still 4.
3. `password KDF` row pattern narrowed with (?!\$) — finding (8b).
4. PASSWORD_MIN/PASSWORD_MAX live in password.js but are ENFORCED in accounts.js. "How long may a password be" is a sign-up rule, not a hashing rule, and putting the check inside hashPassword would have made the unknown-email discard-hash throw for a short password and broken the enumeration property. A10 asserts both bounds through the service.
5. connect R2 rewritten from an HTTP case to a service-level one: with identity from a session and sessions.freelancer_id a foreign key, "an unknown freelancer" is unreachable over HTTP. R8 keeps the reachable 404 (signed in, no connected-account row); R8's unknown-freelancer half was deleted for the same reason.
6. G1 needs a webhook secret configured to see the full route surface (AS-44 registers no route without one). Committed as ALL_ROUTES (14) with G1b asserting the same list minus the webhook route (13) when unconfigured — both directions, so the config-dependence is stated rather than hidden.
7. Recipe naming: my H/G groups combine cases the plan numbered separately (H12–H15 as one test, G9–G12 as one test), so several "EXACT" sets above are one test where the plan named several. No assertion was dropped.

== SPLIT LINES (plan §8) ==
Neither crossed. test/auth.test.js is 958 lines, under the 1,000-line split line, so it stays one file and the harness literal is 14, not 15. test/invoices.test.js is 1,195 against the 1,200 cap — 5 lines of headroom, so no helper extraction was needed. NOTE FOR THE NEXT TASK: plan §11 item 7 said this file was 20 lines from the cap and that a third task hitting it makes splitting a task of its own; it is now 5 lines from the cap. The next task to touch it should expect to extract test/helpers/http.js first.

== AC 26 (evidence required in the record) ==
Measured median in-container scrypt time at the shipped parameters: 40 ms (5 runs: 50,39,40,40,39; the first is cold-start). N=32768 measures 76 ms and throws ERR_CRYPTO_INVALID_SCRYPT_PARAMS under Node's default maxmem — E1/E2/E3 all reproduce. Final line count of test/invoices.test.js: 1,195.
I re-measured every E-row the plan cited before trusting it: E1–E7 reproduce exactly (E4: express 5.2.1, app.router present, app._router absent; E5/E6 emit the exact attribute strings quoted), and E8–E18's greps all matched to the line.

== LEFT UNDONE ==
Nothing in scope. Not done, by design: no push, no merge, no board-owned file edited (plan §10's two proposed wordings for CLAUDE.md and the root README are left for the metawork layer). Flagged for the reviewer and NOT fixed here: finding (2), the absence of any DDL-text assertion in db.test.js — an AS-39-surface change; and plan §11 item 5 (the stack decision's open session/CSRF gap, now answered with zero dependencies) remains a metawork note.

== DOCKER ==
Own project names only (asc-inv-as40, asc-inv-as40-f), profile-aware teardown with --rmi local -v; all three locally-built images removed; stripe/stripe-mock:v0.203.0 left pulled; no global prune. asc-invoicing-web-1 (8348) and asc-chat-server-1 (8347) untouched and still healthy — verified after teardown. The test service kept network_mode: none throughout.

== WHERE A REVIEWER SHOULD START ==
1. app.js's mount order and the boundary banner, then test/auth.test.js G1/G2/G3 — that trio is the whole security claim, and F10 shows the walk alone is not enough.
2. Finding (3) and the two-half structure of A17/A18: that is the difference between the CHECK constraints doing work and being decoration.
3. Findings (8a) and (9) — the two behaviours the plan did not anticipate.
4. Review in the plan's §8 order: migration -> repositories -> lib/auth/* -> routes/auth.js -> app.js -> seam removal -> literal moves.

Orchestrator verification and rulings before review.

IMPERSONATION HOLE — independently verified closed. I grepped the worktree myself rather than taking the report: 'freelancer=' survives in exactly two files, README.md (prose recording the seam as discharged) and test/auth.test.js (G13's attack payload, which must contain it). Zero hits in lib/ or routes/. 'resolveFreelancerId' and 'AS-40 OBLIGATION' survive only in that README sentence. No searchParams.set construction of the parameter remains anywhere. This was the change's single most dangerous requirement and it landed.

SIZE: 30 files, +2636/-250, against a ~2050 projection. Neither pre-agreed split line crossed (auth.test.js 958 of 1000; invoices.test.js 1195 of 1200). No ruling needed.

AC 17 vs AC 20 — TECH-LEAD ITEM, not a rework trigger. The implementer reports the two are mutually exclusive as written: AC 20 requires a test proving the parameter is ignored, which requires the parameter to appear in a test file; AC 17 as worded forbids it appearing anywhere. Production source is at zero for every marker, which is what AC 17 exists to guarantee. Owen should reword AC 17 to scope it to non-test source; the reviewer should judge the implementation against that intent, not against the literal conjunction.

FIFTH RECURRENCE of the assert-baseline defect, and it now has a diagnosis worth acting on. This plan's §7 was written under an explicit instruction to measure every baseline, and one still failed — F2's stated baseline of 1 counted LINES via grep -c where the file has 3 occurrences, because the mount requires an import the count ignored. So the failure mode is not carelessness, it is that grep -c counts lines and recipe authors reason in occurrences. The mechanical fix follows: an assert-applied step must name the line that changes and use an occurrence-accurate count (grep -o | wc -l), or assert on a unique marker introduced by the mutation rather than on a pre-existing token. Adding that to the CLAUDE.md proposal already queued from AS-44.

Review stage: assigning agent:qa-priya. Implementer was Lena, so implementer != reviewer holds, and Ruben reviewed AS-44 — the other security boundary — so alternating keeps both reviewers from becoming the single reader of this app's security surface. Priya also reviewed AS-41 and AS-43, the two tasks whose interim seam this one deletes, which is the right prior context for judging whether the replacement changed their behaviour.

QA REVIEW — AS-40 (qa-priya). Verdict: implementation-level rework needed. 23/26 acceptance criteria pass; AC 3, AC 12 and AC 18 fail.

== READ ORDER (disclosed) ==
1. CLAUDE.md Review Gate + Review Rework Loop; the plan in full (1,461 lines); the task DESCRIPTION alone via `lattice show AS-40 --json` piped through node.
2. The diff cold, in the plan §8 order: migration -> repositories -> lib/auth/* -> routes/auth.js -> app.js -> seam removal -> literal moves. Then the tests as documents.
3. Ran everything myself and wrote my own verdicts and failing sets down FIRST.
4. ONLY THEN the comment stream — Lena's implementation report and Owen's verification comment. Every difference is recorded below in one direction or the other.

== CARDINALITY BEFORE QUANTIFICATION ==
Diff: 30 files, +2636/-250 (10 new, 20 modified). 6 commits. Worktree manifest: 64 files under apps/invoicing.
Suite: 14 test files; 334 reported cases; 316 executed, 18 skipped, 0 fail, exit 0 (`test` service, network_mode: none, mountless).
Contract service: 334 tests, 334 pass, 0 fail, 0 skipped, exit 0 — the 18 un-skip and pass.
V1 self-test (ASC_SELFTEST_MUTATE=1): EXIT=1, as required.
Per-commit: all 6 commits built and run independently — c559bef 287/269/0, 7331874 333/315/0, de52ae8 333/315/0, 51a6206 333/315/0, f878bdd 334/316/0, ff5aae1 334/316/0. Every one green.
Recipes run: 7 (QA-1, QA-2, F4, F7, F8, F10, V4). Attack probes: 8 groups, 45 individual probes.

== BLOCKING FINDING 1 (DEFECT) — `POST /signout` is NOT behind the auth boundary, and G3 cannot tell ==
WHERE: apps/invoicing/app.js:122 mounts `authRoutes` ABOVE the boundary at line 129; apps/invoicing/routes/auth.js:109 defines `router.post('/signout', ...)` inside that same router.
WHAT I DID: drove `POST /signout` with no cookie and a matching Origin.
WHAT HAPPENED: 303, Location `/signin`, AND `Set-Cookie: invoicing_session=; Path=/; Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`. Only `clearSessionCookie` emits that header — so the HANDLER ran. `requireSession` never saw the request.
WHAT SHOULD HAVE HAPPENED: the guard answers, emitting no Set-Cookie — which is what the other eight protected routes do.

PROVEN BY MUTATION (recipe QA-1, mine). Mutation: in a scratch copy, `lib/auth/guard.js` `res.redirect(303, target)` -> `res.redirect(307, target)`. Assert-applied — true OCCURRENCE counts, `grep -o | wc -l`, not line counts: on disk `res.redirect(303, target)` 1 -> 0 and `res.redirect(307, target)` 0 -> 1; in the built image `grep -c 'res.redirect(307, target)' /app/lib/auth/guard.js` = 1. Then enumerated the protected partition:
  GET  /                           307  <- guard
  GET  /connect-stripe/refresh     307  <- guard
  GET  /connect-stripe/return      307  <- guard
  POST /connect-stripe/start       307  <- guard
  POST /invoices                   307  <- guard
  POST /invoices/:id               307  <- guard
  POST /invoices/:id/finalize      307  <- guard
  POST /invoices/:id/send          307  <- guard
  POST /signout                    303  <- HANDLER (1 Set-Cookie)
Eight of nine move with the guard. The ninth does not, because it never reaches it.

WHY IT BLOCKS (not severity, but stated criteria):
- AC 3 requires "a guarded route rejects an absent, invalid, or expired session ... against EVERY route in the protected partition". For POST /signout nothing rejects; the handler accepts and acts.
- AC 18 requires "the public/protected partition is exact in BOTH directions". `PUBLIC_ROUTES` (test/auth.test.js:727) omits POST /signout, so G2 declares it protected. It is public.
- G3 (test/auth.test.js:782) asserts `303` + `Location: /signin`. The signout handler's own success path returns exactly `303` + `/signin`. The assertion is therefore satisfied by the thing it is supposed to be testing the absence of — a vacuous member in the one test the plan calls "the actual proof" (§3.5.2). It would stay green with `requireSession` deleted entirely.
- app.js:119-121 and apps/invoicing/README.md:382 both state the route is "guarded by construction" / "guarded". Both are false, and AS-45 will read them.

SECURITY IMPACT TODAY: low, and I checked rather than assumed. An anonymous POST /signout only clears the caller's own cookie and can only delete the row named by the caller's own cookie — I confirmed a seeded victim's session is still live afterwards. `requireSameOrigin` sits above, so cross-site forced logout is refused. The defect is in the PROOF, not in exploitability — which is exactly the class §3.5 was written to eliminate and the class CLAUDE.md's "a guard is proven by breaking it" convention exists for.

== WHAT THE FIXED TEST NOW REJECTS THAT THE OLD ONE ACCEPTED ==
The old G3 accepted, for every member, ANY response with status 303 and Location '/signin', whatever else it did. What it now accepts is only a response byte-identical, on status, Location and cookie count, to the guard's own live rejection measured in the same app. The residual is unchanged and named in the plan: a future handler that redirects to /signin AND sets no cookie is still indistinguishable in-suite, which is why F12 is a standing recipe re-run whenever the partition changes.
